prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary (max 500 words)

Overall approach
- Ten-year programme to reach net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2030, paired with social and economic reforms. Annual public investment of over £100 billion, plus additional borrowing for capital projects and expected private co‑investment.

Climate, energy and industry
- Rapid expansion of renewables; enable community energy; target ~70% of electricity from wind by 2030; support solar, tidal, hydro, geothermal.
- End fossil-fuel subsidies; escalating Carbon Tax on fossil fuel extraction/imports and embedded emissions; remove oil and gas subsidies; ban fracking; prohibit new nuclear power; expand grid capacity and storage; stronger interconnectors with Europe.
- Industrial transition: clean tech standards, R&D, grants to replace high‑carbon equipment, regional mutual banks, repair/reuse economy, 10‑year warranties/right to repair, reduce fluorinated gases, begin CCS for steel/cement, decommission North Sea assets with a just transition.
- Waste and plastics: ban most single-use plastics; extended producer responsibility; deposit return schemes.

Housing and buildings
- Insulate every home needing it by 2030; deep retrofit 1 million homes/year; renewable heat rollout and heat networks; A‑rating for all rented homes by 2030.
- Build at least 100,000 new social homes/year to Passivhaus-equivalent standards; planning to prefer renovation and sustainable materials.

Transport
- Make public transport cheaper than driving; reopen rail links, electrify main lines; bring rail into public ownership over 10 years; shift freight to rail.
- Give councils bus franchising; invest £2.5bn/yr in cycleways/footpaths; no new runways or increased road capacity; cancel HS2; nationwide EV charging; end sale of new petrol/diesel vehicles by 2030; frequent flyer levy; ban flight advertising; default 20mph residential speed limit.

Food, farming, forestry and nature
- Shift farm subsidies to agroecology; 700 million trees; half of farms in agroforestry by 2030; rewilding support.
- Cut pesticide use by at least 50%; moratorium on GM food; right to food; flood prevention via nature‑based solutions; urban greening; expand protected areas on land and sea; create Environmental Protection Commission; ecocide law.

Income, work and housing security
- Phase in Universal Basic Income: adults £89/week; pensioners £178/week; supplements for disabled people, lone parents and children; retain Housing Benefit where needed.
- Living Wage £12/hour including ages 16–21; close gig‑economy loopholes; cap top pay at 10x lowest; rent controls; end no‑fault evictions; expand community ownership; explore shorter working week; 35 hours/week free childcare from 9 months.

Democracy and governance
- Proportional representation for all elections; votes at 16; fully elected second chamber; party funding reform; tighter lobbying and media ownership rules; Digital Bill of Rights; citizens’ assemblies; stronger local government with +£10bn/yr funding, £3bn/yr climate adaptation, and free home care at home for over‑65s.

EU and international
- A confirmatory referendum on any Brexit deal with an option to remain; EU reforms for transparency, citizen initiative, social and environmental standards; uphold freedom of movement; EU carbon border measures; increase aid to 1% of GNI focused on climate and poverty; fair trade conditions; end investor‑state dispute mechanisms.

Public services
- NHS: +£6bn/yr rising to 2030; end internal market; expand community and mental health; free contraception; PrEP provision.
- Education: +£4bn/yr; reduce class sizes; start formal schooling at 6; restore local democratic oversight; scrap tuition fees; write off debt from £9k-fee regime; expand adult and further education; climate and nature curricula.

Justice, drugs, discrimination, animals
- Halve prison population long-term via prevention, restorative justice, youth services; community policing.
- Replace prohibition with regulated drug markets; pardon past possession/low‑level supply offences; heroin-assisted treatment; legal cannabis with licensing; minimum alcohol pricing.
- Strategies against discrimination; humane immigration with an end to indefinite detention; retain Human Rights Act; measures on hate crime and gender-based violence; strengthen LGBTIQA+ and disability rights.
- Animal sentience law; ban hunting and snares; end badger cull; stricter transport limits; end cages; reduce animal testing; method-of-production labelling; Commission on Animal Protection.

Tax and funding
- Carbon Tax (~£76.7bn/yr); consolidate and simplify income/wealth taxes; equalise tax on income from work and wealth; move towards Land Value Tax replacing Council Tax/Business Rates (phased over 10 years); Corporation Tax to 24%; independent HMRC; anti‑avoidance measures; legalised drug tax revenues.
- Cancel Trident replacement, major new roads, airport expansions, HS2; redirect funds to low‑carbon transport. Operational spend increase ~£141.5bn/yr funded by tax changes and savings; capital spend ~£94.4bn/yr via borrowing.
